Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-26
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Sam Keller (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM); Maya Chen, Liam Ortiz, Sofia Patel, Ethan Ruiz (Orion Retail Labs)

Summary: Quick QBR-style checkin focused on cost and reliability; agreed to pilot and data share

Transcript body:
[00:00] Sam Keller: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll kick off — Jordan, quick intro?
[00:08] Jordan Lee: yeah thanks, hey team at Orion, Sam and Priya from Red wood, Jordan CSM, we'll run through the Q4 pri orti - prioritization and cost triage, hope that's ok.
[00:18] Maya Chen: yep that sounds good, tight on time today so appreciate it.
[00:24] Sam Keller: quick agenda — short recap of last quarter usage and the spike that caused the 09 slash 23 degradation, then cost model options (dedicated vs hosted), security questions, and decide pilot scope.
[00:36] Priya Nair: I'll do a brief of the incident root cause and the perf numbers we saw — some of the numbers are in the deck I just dropped into the chat: https://redwood.com/teams/orion/qbr-deck and there's the spreadsheet link for TCO: https://redwood.com/teams/orion/tco-2027-q4.xlsx
[00:50] Liam Ortiz: got it thanks, I can open that after. The big thing for us is — latency spikes during peak checkout flow, customers noticed lag. We need sub-200ms tail ideally.
[01:02] Priya Nair: right, and during the event the system hit an unexpected tail because of KV cache misses and a backlog of long-context requests, plus autoscaler lag — so throughput dropped. The fix in the short term was to increase burst capacity and patch the autoscaler rules.
[01:20] Maya Chen: when you say K V cache, was that like our prefix cache? We saw repeated recompute for some sessions.
[01:26] Priya Nair: yeah the prefix/K V behaved like it wasn't hitting due to slightly different session ids — small tokenization mismatch, ironically. That cost you extra tokens.
[01:36] Ethan Ruiz: and to confirm, were those requests routed to the hosted pool? or dedicated?
[01:41] Sam Keller: mostly hosted at the time — your prod rollout was on hosted. We suggested a dedicated pool for the shopping-assistant because of the latency SLOs, but we wanted to run numbers with you first.
[01:50] Sofia Patel: speaking of numbers, our spend jumped ~42% month over month with that spike. We need to see dedicated vs hosted TCO — if dedicated is 20% cheaper at scale we can justify it, otherwise we can't.
[02:05] Priya Nair: fair. The spreadsheet has scenarios: baseline, +25% traffic, +200% traffic (flash sale). For dedicated we show reserved GPU commit plus burst credits; hosted shows per-token with priority bumping. There are also ops impacts (on-call, patching) listed.
[02:22] Liam Ortiz: one question — what about quantization? We heard Redwood Optima — um Redwood Optimize — recommended configs. Are those going to materially affect quality?
[02:33] Priya Nair: yes, we have quant profiles per model. At +-4bit we saw <2% quality drift on your eval set for the shopping assistant tasks, but latency cut by ~35%. We'll include the eval runs in the test harness.
[02:46] Maya Chen: is that something we can test in a pilot with 1-2 models?
[02:50] Priya Nair: absolutely, pilot plan can include: 1) dedicated small pool with quant profile A, 2) hosted canary with same config, and 3) baseline to compare. We'll run A/B traffic using your traces.
[03:05] Sofia Patel: on security — we need KMS integration and audit logs sent to our SIEM, plus SSO/SAML for console access. Can Redwood do HSM-backed keys?
[03:17] Sam Keller: yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and audit log streaming. For hosted we have envelope encryption with BYOK options; I'll flag Priya to share the security pack. Link: https://redwood.com/security/orion-pack.pdf
[03:30] Ethan Ruiz: data residency — some EU requests must remain in eu-west-1. How flexible is routing?
[03:36] Priya Nair: routing policies can pin by region and we can set fallbacks. For Private deployments there is full region control. For Hosted, we can guarantee region routing for the pilot under the SLA.
[03:48] Maya Chen: timeline — product wants to ship the assistant in mid-December. What's a realistic path if we start pilot Nov 9?
[03:55] Sam Keller: pilot kickoff Nov 9, 2-week benchmark window, then canary rollout week of Nov 23, scale tests early Dec, final rollout mid-Dec — that aligns if there are no surprises.
[04:08] Liam Ortiz: ok, and SLAs — do we get latency SLOs in writing for dedicated pools?
[04:13] Jordan Lee: yes dedicated comes with a latency SLA tier; we'll include the SLOs and a fallback policy (auto-route to hosted compatible variant) in the pilot plan.
[04:24] Sofia Patel: about budgeting — what's the minimum commit for Dedicated? We don't want to overcommit.
[04:29] Sam Keller: typical entry is a monthly reserved pool equivalent to X GPUs (we'll define numbers in the TCO). We can propose a smaller reserve plus burst coverage to limit commit risk.
[04:40] Maya Chen: anything else on the incident learnings?
[04:44] Priya Nair: ops playbook update: better tokenization alignment checks pre-rollout, prefix cache key normalization, and aggressive warmup of KV cache before high traffic windows. We'll add those to runbook and propose test hooks.
[04:58] Ethan Ruiz: sounds good — can Priya share the exact test harness steps we can run in staging?
[05:02] Priya Nair: yes will send. It uses your traces and runs 3x stress passes with increasing context length. We'll include scripts and sample config.
[05:12] Maya Chen: ok let's talk acceptance criteria for the pilot — what constitutes success?
[05:16] Sam Keller: suggested criteria: 1) P50/P95 latency improvement vs baseline (target <200ms P95), 2) Cost per 1k requests within agreed threshold, 3) No critical errors for 48h at peak load, 4) Quality regression <2% on our eval set.
[05:31] Sofia Patel: I want that cost clause in writing — we will not sign off unless costs are within guardrails.
[05:36] Sam Keller: understood, we'll quantify in the TCO and annotate risk scenarios.
[05:42] Liam Ortiz: on telemetry, we need token-level cost breakdowns and per-request traces. Can redwood expose that?
[05:49] Jordan Lee: yes, Redwood Console has token-level and per-route dashboards and we can grant read access to your infra engineers. We'll also expose a trace export API.
[05:58] Maya Chen: ok next steps recap?
[06:02] Sam Keller: quick recap: Sam to send annotated TCO + deck by Nov 2; Priya to deliver test harness + quant eval by Nov 5; Orion to send traces by Nov 4; schedule pilot kickoff Nov 9. Anyone object?
[06:15] Sofia Patel: no objections, just please highlight the worst-case cost scenario in the sheet.
[06:20] Sam Keller: will do. Anything else from Orion?
[06:24] Ethan Ruiz: can you attach the previous incident postmortem with root cause? I missed some details.
[06:29] Priya Nair: yes, I'll attach the postmortem to the ticket and share the runbook updates.
[06:35] Maya Chen: that's all for us. Thanks everyone.
[06:38] Sam Keller: thanks team, we'll follow up with items and calendar invites. Bye.
[06:43] Jordan Lee: thanks all, talk soon.

End of transcript. Note: transcription contains minor recognition errors (names, acronyms).
